analysis.title: UBS Daily Consumer/Lux 10 Nov: Henkel; M&S; WOSG (+ve); Carlsberg; Ahold Delhaize
key_insights: European equities opened with the EStoxx up 90bps as crude fell to its lowest since August (Brent $91.7, WTI $86.2) after President Trump said 'Iran, militarily, is effectively over'.

US AI value chain rebounded sharply on Monday, with Semis, Neoclouds and AI Winners up 6-7%. SPX rose 2.35% and breadth barely changed, which the desk reads as more risk-on than pure relief. It expects mild underperformance in Defensives over coming sessions.

Asia followed the US tech rebound: Topix and Taiex +2-3%, KOSPI +5%, SoftBank about +15% ahead of earnings. Taiwan October exports hit a record of +58.9% y/y versus +51% estimated, and TSMC October revenue was NT586.9bn (+51% MoM).

UBS Strategy says positioning is now considerably cleaner. Risk Control exposure at 55% is the lowest since the tariff washout, and the last two comparable resets (Aug-24, Apr-25) were followed by 17% and 24% rises in the S&P over four months. CTA equity exposure has turned negative (-5%).

The desk argues the systematic feedback loop that amplifies headline-driven selling has largely been removed, with real money not selling and corporate buybacks returning next week. Short-term sentiment is still described as fragile, and a more durable AI demand recovery likely depends on ECM/DCM pipeline milestones.

US CPI is due this afternoon. UBS US Econ expects headline 0.26% m/m (consensus 0.29%, UBS Nowcast 0.32%) and core 0.23% (Bloomberg consensus 0.24%, Nowcast 0.22%). Goods prices are cooling (Adobe online prices, JD Power used-car prices) while services inflation stays sticky.

Henkel Q3 and the guidance upgrade were already pre-announced, so the print was in line. Q3 group organic sales growth was +6.5% (pricing +5.4%, volume +1.1%). IMEA grew +27.8% versus VA consensus of +9.3%, nearly half of group growth, while Europe (+2.2%) missed consensus of +4.2%.

Henkel FY26 guidance is organic growth of +3.0-4.0% and adj. EBIT margin of about 15.0%, in line with consensus. The conference call (8am UKT) will focus on Q4 exit rates, sustainability of Q3 pricing, Adhesives destocking after customer pre-buy, and price-cost recovery.

M&S capital markets day targets were seen as mixed. The >10% FH&B margin target is already in FY27 estimates, and the ~5% Food margin ambition is below current expectations (VA cons 5.6%, UBSe 5.4%). The incremental positive is profit growing ahead of sales, £600m cost savings by FY28 and a doubled dividend to 8.4p.

Watches of Switzerland gave a better-than-expected trading update and raised the low end of FY27 guidance (OSG +7-10% versus +5-10% before, adj EBIT margin +60-80bps versus +40-80bps). UBS raised EPS estimates by 2% and PT to 898p from 890p, calling H2 assumptions prudent.

WOSG H1 constant-currency growth was +15% versus consensus +11%. US grew +22% (about 50% of sales and 60% of EBIT) and UK/Europe +9% versus consensus +4%. 1H27 adj EBIT is guided to £87-89m versus consensus £81m.
Delfin (EssilorLuxottica's holding company) is working on a flexible 10 billion buyback open to all Del Vecchio family shareholders, allowing partial and staged exits.
Hugo Boss Chief Sales Officer and Deputy CEO Oliver Timm leaves at end of November. UBS sees limited earnings impact but added uncertainty around strategic direction after recent management turnover.

UBS PrimeView: Food/Beverages/Tobacco stays net short (L/S ratio about 0.75) and is the 4th most negatively crowded sector. HPC stays net long but its L/S ratio fell to about 2.2 from 2.8. Consumer Durables & Apparel L/S ticked up to about 1.25 on short covering.

Luxury crowding: most crowded longs are Richemont, Burberry, LVMH, Watches of Switzerland and Pandora. Most crowded shorts are Kering, Brunello Cucinelli, Zegna, Moncler and Hugo Boss, and Moncler newly entered the short-crowded list. Conviction in these scores is described as low.

Somnigroup reported 3Q adjusted EPS of $1.04 versus UBS $1.06 and consensus $1.05 and cut FY26 EPS guidance to $2.85-2.95 from $2.95-3.25. Management's first 2027 framework is about $3.40 EPS in a flat industry, well below pre-results consensus of $3.93. UBS cut its FY27 EPS estimate to $3.50.

BellRing reports F4Q on 11/18 before the open. UBS calls the setup difficult, with valuation attractive but FY27 visibility poor (pricing, commodity and logistics costs, competition, new CEO). It would wait for clarity before turning more constructive.

US hardlines retail: UBS sees HD and LOW Q3 prints as a test of earnings resilience, with Q3 comps forecast at +1.5% for HD and flat for LOW and FY26 guidance maintained. FY27 profitability is the bigger question as tariff-refund benefits roll off. Both are Buy rated with PTs of $420 and $275.

Earnings previews: Gap 3Q sales forecast +2.8% y/y versus consensus +1.9% with EPS $0.78 in line, options imply an 11.0% move versus 9.0% historical, and UBS expects less. TJX Q3 EPS is seen roughly in line with the $1.34 Street figure and options imply 4.6% versus 3.3% historical, which UBS agrees with. Wolverine is expected to beat by 2c and raise guidance by about that amount.

UBS Global Economics outlook: US real consumption grew 2.5% y/y through September on equity-market wealth (almost 40% of household net worth) despite negative real wage growth. UBS forecasts real PCE growth of 2.6% in 2026, 2.2% in 2027 and 2.4% in 2028, as a roughly $60 billion tax-refund boost fades in 2027. China consumption growth is expected to stay broadly stable.

Carlsberg agreed to sell Britvic Brazil for EUR 80m, expected to close by December 2026. Botswana plans to double its stake in De Beers to 30% and the Gareth Penny consortium is backed as bidder for Anglo American's 85% holding.

Phillips' Geneva watch auction generated CHF92m ($112.3m), the first live watch sale above $100m, with all 217 lots sold. Pandora closed four French and Spanish stores during protests, hurting a nascent European sales rebound (France is about 4% of sales).

Carlsberg agreed to sell Britvic Brazil for EUR 80m after a strategic review, closing by December 2026.
Ahold Delhaize rated Neutral. News flow was Alfa Beta selling ENA Cash & Carry and Food Lion buying five Winn-Dixie stores. It saw the largest negative crowding change in EU Retail.

earnings_insights: Henkel Q3 pre-announced, reported basis organic sales growth +6.5% (pricing +5.4%, volume +1.1%). Consumer Brands +4.8%, Adhesive Technologies +7.9%. By region IMEA +27.8% vs VA cons +9.3%, Europe +2.2% vs cons +4.2%, North America +3.4% vs cons +2.1%, Asia Pacific +8.9% vs cons +3.0%.

Henkel FY26 guidance (already pre-announced): group organic growth +3.0-4.0% (VA cons +3.3%, UBSe +4.0%), adj. EBIT margin about 15.0% (VA cons 14.9%), adj. EPS growth mid-single-digit cFX (VA cons and UBSe +3.8%).

Watches of Switzerland trading update (reported): H1 FY27 cFX growth +15% vs cons +11% and UBSe +13%. 1H27 adj. EBIT pre-IFRS 16 guided £87-89m vs cons £81m. FY27 outlook c.FX growth +7-10% (cons +9%), margin expansion +60-80bp (cons +65bp), capex £60-£70m (cons £69m).

Somnigroup 3Q adjusted EPS reported $1.04 vs UBS est $1.06 and consensus $1.05. FY26 EPS guidance cut to $2.85-2.95 from $2.95-3.25. Management 2027 framework about $3.40 EPS in a flat industry, each point of industry growth adds about $0.10. Pre-results consensus FY27 EPS was $3.93 and UBS now estimates $3.50.
BellRing F4Q26 (estimate, not yet printed) is scheduled for 11/18 before the open. UBS expects a decent F4Q but low FY27 visibility, and management may build flexibility into its initial outlook.
Wolverine World Wide Q3 (not yet printed): UBS anticipates a 2c EPS beat and an in-line Q4 outlook, with FY EPS guidance of $1.55-$1.65 likely raised by about the Q3 beat.
Gap 3Q26 preview (UBS est): sales +2.8% y/y vs +1.9% consensus, EPS $0.78 broadly in line with consensus, unchanged FY26 guidance. Options imply +/-11.0% event move vs 9.0% historical average.

TJX Q3 preview (UBS est): roughly in-line EPS vs the Street's $1.34 forecast, Marmaxx comp +1% vs Street +1.8%, FY27 guidance expected to rise to $5.18-$5.23 from $5.15-$5.20. Options imply +/-4.6% vs 3.3% historical average.
HD and LOW Q3 preview (UBS est): comps +1.5% for HD and flat for LOW, both expected to maintain FY26 guidance. FY27 profitability is the key issue as tariff-refund benefits roll off.

M&S capital markets day targets: Food operating margin about 5% (FY27E VA cons 5.6%, UBSe 5.4%) and FH&B margin above 10% (FY27E VA cons 10.2%, UBSe 10.5%). FY27 sales growth Food +9.3% (VA cons) and FH&B +9.5% (VA cons, UBSe +7.8%).
Burberry H1 preview (Nov 12) UBS in line with consensus. Richemont Q2 preview (Nov 13) UBS ahead of consensus. On Holding post-earnings feedback call today at 12:30pm ET.

French officials suspect Iran was behind the October 11 cyberattack that overrode temperature controls on commercial fridges in hundreds of establishments. Iran routinely denies cyber operations.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS Strategy says positioning is considerably cleaner. Risk Control exposure at 55% is the lowest since the tariff washout and past resets were followed by 17% and 24% S&P gains over four months. Buybacks return next week and systematic supply is largely exhausted.
tension_points.bear_case: Short-term sentiment remains fragile and the desk says a durable AI demand recovery depends on ECM/DCM pipeline milestones. US CPI today is a near-term risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hot US CPI print this afternoon or a renewed headline-driven selloff in the AI complex would undermine the cleaner-positioning thesis.

tension_points.bull_case: Profit growth ahead of sales, £600m cost savings by FY28, positive FCF in each of the next three years and a doubled dividend support the story.
tension_points.bear_case: The ~5% Food margin target is below current expectations (VA cons 5.6%, UBSe 5.4%), so the Food opportunity depends more on sustained sales and share growth than margin expansion.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Food sales growth falling short of the +9.3% FY27 consensus would weaken the Food case.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS stays Buy rated and sees its $3.50 FY27 EPS estimate as modestly above management's $3.40 floor, with every point of industry growth adding about $0.10 of EPS.
tension_points.bear_case: Pre-results consensus FY27 EPS of $3.93 appeared to require mid-single-digit industry growth, which UBS believes is too aggressive. FY26 guidance was cut.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Industry growth running at mid-single digits in 2027 would validate the old consensus of $3.93.

tension_points.bull_case: Valuation is very attractive relative to long-term growth, top-line growth is ahead of most Staples, and tracked trends are stronger than expected.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors focus on FY27 given pricing, elevated commodity and logistics costs, unfavorable competition and a new CEO, so conviction on near-term trajectory is hard.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Greater clarity on the FY27 earnings trajectory with the F4Q report on 11/18 would make UBS more constructive.

tension_points.theme: HD and LOW into Q3 prints
tension_points.bull_case: Home improvement demand appears to have bottomed with repair-and-maintenance and Pro demand supporting sales. Valuation of about 22x and 17x CY27E P/E looks favorable.
tension_points.bear_case: Housing turnover keeps declining, rates are elevated and larger discretionary projects remain under pressure. FY27 profitability faces tariff-refund roll-off and elevated fuel and freight costs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: FY26 guidance not being maintained, or FY27 profit commentary pointing to margin pressure, would undermine the thesis.
